catalyst_text: First participant dosed in Phase 1 study
detailed_catalyst_text: The first participant was dosed in a Phase 1, first-in-human study of a prophylactic vaccine candidate in healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years. The study is designed to assess safety and tolerability with secondary immunogenicity measures to support advancement for prevention of Group A Streptococcus infections.
catalyst_text_evidence: Vaxcyte, Inc. (NASDAQ:PCVX), a clinical-stage vaccine innovation company engineering high-fidelity vaccines to protect humankind from bacterial diseases, today announced that the first participant was dosed in the Phase 1, first-in-human study evaluating VAX-A1, the Company's investigational prophylactic vaccine candidate for the prevention of disease caused by Group A Streptococcus (Group A Strep), in healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years.

drug_indication: Invasive pneumococcal disease and pneumonia in adults
catalyst_text: Completed enrollment in two pivotal Phase 3 trials
detailed_catalyst_text: Enrollment was completed for the pivotal OPUS-1 Phase 3 noninferiority study (~4,000 adults) and the OPUS-2 Phase 3 concomitant administration study (~1,300 adults), evaluating safety, tolerability and immunogenicity in adults. These milestones advance development for prevention of invasive pneumococcal disease and pneumonia in adults and support progress toward forthcoming readouts and a potential BLA submission.
catalyst_text_evidence: SAN CARLOS, Calif., 2026-03-23 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vaxcyte, Inc. (NASDAQ:PCVX), a clinical-stage vaccine innovation company, today announced the completion of enrollment in the VAX-31 OPUS-1 Phase 3 pivotal, noninferiority trial with approximately 4,000 participants and the OPUS-2 Phase 3 trial evaluating VAX-31 concomitantly administered with a seasonal influenza vaccine in approximately 1,300 participants. The pivotal Phase 3 study of VAX-31 is now fully enrolled with approximately 4,000 adults. This Phase 3 study, which is now fully enrolled with approximately 1,300 adults, is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability and immunogenicity of VAX-31 when administered either concomitantly with or one month following administration of a licensed seasonal influenza vaccine in pneumococcal-naïve, healthy U.S. adults aged 50 years and older.

catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 3 trial dosing first participants
detailed_catalyst_text: First participants were dosed in the OPUS-3 Phase 3 study evaluating adults who previously received pneumococcal vaccination. The trial measures safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity to assess boosting potential and broadened serotype coverage in this pre-vaccinated adult population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Vaxcyte, Inc. (NASDAQ:PCVX), a clinical-stage vaccine innovation company, today announced that the first participants were dosed in the OPUS-3 Phase 3 trial evaluating VAX-31, the Company's next-generation 31-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) candidate, in adults who have previously received pneumococcal vaccination. This trial is evaluating the safety, tolerability and immunogenicity of VAX-31, including whether VAX-31 can boost serotype-specific immune responses, while providing the broadest coverage in a single vaccine in this adult population.

drug_indication: Invasive pneumococcal disease and pneumonia in adults
catalyst_text: Phase 3 trial initiated with first participants dosed
detailed_catalyst_text: First participants were dosed in the OPUS pivotal Phase 3 noninferiority trial evaluating prevention of invasive pneumococcal disease and pneumonia in adults. The randomized, double-blind, active-controlled study includes head-to-head comparisons versus PCV21 and PCV20 to assess safety, tolerability and immunogenicity.
catalyst_text_evidence: Vaxcyte, Inc. (NASDAQ:PCVX), a clinical-stage vaccine innovation company, today announced that the first participants were dosed in the OPUS (OPA-based Pivotal U.S. Study) Phase 3 pivotal, noninferiority trial evaluating VAX-31 for the prevention of invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) and pneumonia in adults.
